# Unconstrained

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

Renders its child outside the flow: the child draws from the current cursor position but consumes no height, so whatever follows starts where the child started.

It is the escape hatch for content that should overlap rather than stack - a badge over a table, a rubber stamp across a paragraph, a rule drawn behind the next few lines. The child is measured as zero-height, which also means it never triggers a page break of its own and never splits: it renders once, here, and anything past the page boundary is clipped by the page.

Because the cursor does not move, two `Unconstrained` siblings draw on top of each other. That is the point, but it makes the element easy to misuse - reach for it only when overlap is what you want.

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`. Extends `PaginationWrapperBase`.

## Constructors

```typescript
new Unconstrained()
new Unconstrained(options: UnconstrainedOptions)
new Unconstrained(child: IElement)
```
